evidence_summary: Medium-confidence signals: (1) Better Mortgage LOs report 2.7/5 stars compensation satisfaction on Glassdoor, citing reduced splits and tighter control vs. 2025 (https://www.glassdoor.com/Reviews/Better-Mortgage-Loan-Officer-Reviews, 2026-02); (2) Market shift: Glassdoor reporting large lenders raising internal fees, reducing splits in 2026 (https://www.glassdoor.com/Job/san-francisco-mortgage-loan-officer-jobs, 2026-02); (3) Better Mortgage facing comp structure pressure across LO teams. Compensation push factor; monitor for active job search signals.

High-confidence company turmoil + moderate team signal: (1) Country Club Mortgage laid off 100+ employees including C-suite and shuttered offices due to facility closures per HousingWire (https://www.housingwire.com/articles/country-club-mortgage-to-lay-off-employees-including-ceo-and-shutter-offices/, Jan 2024, high confidence); (2) LA metro is primary market for CCM historically, likely impact on local team; (3) Post-acquisition/restructuring period creates job search window. Strong push factor: major employer instability.

Mixed-confidence regulatory signal: (1) Fairway Independent Mortgage under CFPB and Justice Department enforcement action (https://www.fairway.com/press-release/fairway-independent-mortgage-responds-to-cfpb-and-justice-department-announcement, Oct 2024, high confidence); (2) Regulatory scrutiny creates internal uncertainty and potential org changes; (3) No direct open-to-work signal observed, but regulatory pressure is moderate push. Watchlist candidate; monitor for policy/comp changes or departures announcement.

Medium-confidence team and market-condition signals: (1) Sacramento market showing 24 MLO job openings on Glassdoor (https://www.glassdoor.com/Job/sacramento-mortgage-loan-officer-jobs, Feb 2026, medium confidence), indicating hiring pressure and talent mobility; (2) Independent brokerages facing margin compression and increased competition per market data; (3) Profile update activity and peer departures signal transition considerations. Moderate dissatisfaction signals; competitive market conditions creating openness to opportunity.

Low-confidence mixed signals: (1) Guild Mortgage post-acquisition from Interactive/WinnPointe, now integrated operation (https://www.thetruthaboutmortgage.com/a-list-of-recent-mortgage-closures-mergers-and-layoffs/, historical context, medium confidence); (2) Guild Mortgage rated A+ BBB, fewer CFPB complaints than average (https://themortgagereports.com/68796/guild-mortgage-review-rates-loans-credit-score, May 2025, high confidence on company stability); (3) San Diego strong market, minimal branch closure risk. Stable employer; no strong push signals. Low priority unless macro conditions shift.
